source_refs.note: Topic 2.2.1.5 Handling Integer and Float Inputs (PDF 37, printed 34). The printed code is garbled in places ('Ent er'); the lesson gives a cleaned version.

blocks.text: input() always returns text. To use the input as a number, convert it with int() for whole numbers or float() for decimal numbers.

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
# Integer input
user_age = int(input("Enter your age: "))
print("Your age is:", user_age)
# Float input
user_height = float(input("Enter your height in meters: "))
print("Your height is", user_height, "meters")

blocks.prompt: What happens if the user types 1.75 when the program calls int(input(...))?
blocks.explanation: int() cannot convert the text '1.75', so Python raises a ValueError; float(input(...)) should be used for decimal values.

items: Convert input text with int() for whole numbers and float() for decimals.
